explanation: FRELIMO made this argument itself and most accounts of the war repeat it. Mueda ended the case for petitioning. The Makonde cooperative movement had taken a demand to the administration and had been shot at for it, and the men who founded the nationalist parties out of which FRELIMO was assembled in 1962 came from that world. The edge does not claim a straight line. Three exile parties built the movement in Tanganyika, on the Cold War's terms as much as on Mueda's, and the toll at Mueda is disputed. After 1960 nobody in the north argued for petitioning again.
